findings.title: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds a display config and then discards it
findings.description:
Lines 160-162 copy `monitor.config` and replace `schedule_type` with `get_schedule_type_display()`. Line 168 then returns `monitor_environment.monitor.config`, the raw dict, so the local `config` is dead code.

- **Effect:** the occurrence's monitor context carries the integer `schedule_type` instead of the display string.
- **Inconsistent with:** `src/sentry/monitors/serializers.py:242`, which performs the same substitution and uses the result.
- **Pinned by a test:** `tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py:119` asserts `"schedule_type": 2`, so the fix must update that expectation.
- **Origin:** pre-existing, moved unchanged from `mark_failed.py`.

Fix: return `"config": config`, or delete the three dead lines if the raw value is intended.

findings.title: `get_failure_reason` docstring contradicts its output
findings.description:
- **Wrong examples:** the docstring shows "…were detected" and "A failed check-in was detected". The code only produces "%(problem_checkins)s check-ins detected" (line 156) or the three strings in `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP`.
- **Typo:** "humam readible".
- **Undercounting:** statuses outside `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP` are silently dropped from the count. The threshold query at `incidents.py:40-44` only excludes on `OK`, so an `IN_PROGRESS` row inside the window makes the message report fewer check-ins than the threshold evaluated.

findings.title: Occurrence loop re-fetches rows, repeats per-item queries, and has no ordering
findings.description:
- **Unordered:** `MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(id__in=...)` has no `order_by`, so occurrences are produced in database order. The oldest-first ordering established at line 48 is lost.
- **Repeated queries:** each `create_incident_occurrence` call re-runs `monitor_env.get_last_successful_checkin()` (`incident_occurrence.py:46`, an uncached query per `models.py:707-712`) and resolves `get_environment()` twice.
- **Suggested fix:** add `.order_by("date_added")` and hoist the last-successful lookup out of the loop.
- **Origin:** pre-existing behaviour, moved unchanged.

findings.title: Status flip and incident creation are not atomic
findings.description: `monitor_env.status = ERROR` is saved before `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)`, with no transaction around the pair. If the create fails, the environment stays `ERROR` with no active incident. Later failures then take the `elif` branch at line 72, get `active_incident = None`, and skip occurrences at line 92 without logging. Pre-existing, but now the core of a module named for incident handling.

findings.title: Unused loggers and loose typing in the new modules
findings.description:
- **Unused loggers:** `logger` is defined but never used in `incidents.py:11`, `incident_occurrence.py:25`, and (after the extraction) `mark_failed.py:11`.
- **Missing return annotations:** `get_failure_reason` and `get_monitor_environment_context`.
- **Misleading cast:** `cast(list[SimpleCheckIn], <QuerySet>)` at `incidents.py:37-45` labels a lazy `QuerySet` as a list.
- **Minor:** `any([...])` at line 52 builds an unnecessary list.

findings.title: No tests accompany the new modules
findings.description: `try_incident_threshold`, `create_incident_occurrence` and `get_failure_reason` are covered only indirectly through `mark_failed()` in `test_mark_failed.py`. There is no `test_incidents.py` or `test_incident_occurrence.py`. This is acceptable for a pure move, but `get_failure_reason` has no direct unit test for its mixed-status and plural branches.

findings.title: Refactor is behaviour-preserving with no dangling references
findings.description:
- **Bodies unchanged:** the moved functions are byte-identical to the removed ones apart from the two renames (`mark_failed_threshold` → `try_incident_threshold`, `create_issue_platform_occurrence` → `create_incident_occurrence`).
- **No stale references:** a repo-wide grep finds no remaining uses of the old monitor names. The `create_issue_platform_occurrence` hits are the unrelated `sentry.uptime` function.
- **External importers unaffected:** `check_missed.py`, `check_timeout.py`, `monitor_consumer.py` and the tests import only `mark_failed`.
- **No import cycle:** `SimpleCheckIn` now lives in `monitors/types.py`, and `types.py` does not import `models`.
- **Test patch still valid:** tests patch `sentry.issues.producer.produce_occurrence_to_kafka`, which still works because `incident_occurrence.py:35` keeps the function-local import.
- **Side benefit:** the `incident, _ = ...` unpack in `incidents.py:62` no longer shadows a module-level gettext `_`.

structured_findings.summary: `get_monitor_environment_context` builds a display config and then discards it
Occurrence loop re-fetches rows, repeats per-item queries, and has no ordering
Status flip and incident creation are not atomic
Unused loggers and loose typing in the new modules
No tests accompany the new modules
Refactor is behaviour-preserving with no dangling references
